forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No change from yesterday's 21%. AGI-timeline discourse this week reaffirmed near-term insider views (Amodei: powerful AI late-2026/2027; Altman: 'research interns' within a year, independent researchers ~2028; Shane Legg: 50% minimal AGI by 2028), but none of these meets the resolution bar of a credible lab declaring AGI achieved, or 3+ leading researchers stating so. The bar remains unmet.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative-technology arrival inside a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders have strong optimism incentives. Historically such forecasts resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab CEO timelines (Amodei, Altman, Legg) cluster at 2027-2028, partly inside the window
Rapid capability and capital momentum; OpenAI IPO filing signals continued scale-up

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (clean credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
Persistent generality/agentic shortfalls keep a 'declared AGI' event unlikely before 2030

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will use the term 'AGI' in a formal declaration versus avoiding it
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved'
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if frontier progress visibly plateaus or labs explicitly disavow near-term AGI

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 25%. June 2026 evidence continues to show AI-driven restructuring across consulting (McKinsey cutting ~10% of staff, 3,000-4,000 roles; Accenture, KPMG, PwC, EY, Deloitte, Bain also cutting since 2023), with cuts concentrated in junior/research roles where generative AI compresses delivery. But a ≥33% decline in revenue OR employment, primarily attributed to AI by 2+ credible analyses, remains a high bar — current cuts are ~10% and partly cyclical (discretionary-spend slowdown, boutique competition).
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: incumbent professional-services sectors facing a general-purpose technology shock over a ~4-year horizon. Sectors rarely shed a third of value/employment that fast and with clean single-cause attribution; base ~10-15%.

factors_up.factor: Visible, accelerating AI-linked layoffs at multiple top firms; pyramid model eroding from the base
Boutique AI-native advisory competition compounding AI productivity pressure

factors_down.factor: ≥33% is a steep threshold; firms are repricing/reskilling rather than collapsing
Attribution 'primarily to AI' is contested — cyclical demand and rate effects confound it

key_uncertainties: Whether revenue (not just headcount) falls ≥33%, and the baseline definition used
Whether 2+ credible analyses attribute the decline primarily to AI rather than the cycle
update_triggers: Revise UP if a major firm reports double-digit revenue decline explicitly blamed on AI
Revise DOWN if consulting revenues stabilise or rebound through 2027

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 5%. The 17 June 2026 PollCheck 7-poll average has Reform UK leading on 26.9%, with Labour (19.3%) and the Conservatives (19.1%) effectively tied for second. Reform has led voting intention since late 2025. With the next GE not due until 2029, recovery is possible, but on current standings Labour being the largest party is a low-probability outcome.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing parties polling ~7pp behind the leader mid-term, ~3 years from an election. Such parties recover to 'largest party' a minority of the time; base ~20-30%, adjusted down for the unusually fragmented 5-party split and Reform's durable lead.

factors_up.factor: ~3 years to the election leaves ample time for reversion and incumbency tools
FPTP + fragmented opposition vote can convert a modest Labour recovery into most seats

factors_down.factor: Reform holds a durable ~8pp lead sustained for over six months
Labour third in vote share in some polls; no clear recovery trend yet

key_uncertainties: Timing of the next GE and whether Labour's polling recovers before it
How vote share converts to seats under FPTP given a 5-way split
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour regains a polling lead or moves clearly into first
Revise DOWN if Reform's lead widens further or Labour falls consistently to third

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 81%. The longer 9.5-year window comfortably contains the clustered 2027-2028 insider timelines plus substantial slack for slippage. June 2026 discourse (Amodei, Altman, Legg, OpenAI's 'AGI researchers by 2028' roadmap) is consistent with a high but not near-certain probability that the resolution bar is met sometime before 2035.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: probability that a rapidly advancing GPT-class technology reaches a declared human-level milestone within ~10 years. Long-horizon expert aggregations (Metaculus, surveys) cluster well above 50% for this window; base ~70-80%.

factors_up.factor: Insider median timelines (2027-2028) sit far inside the window with years of slack
Sustained compute, capital and algorithmic progress lower the chance of a decade-long stall

factors_down.factor: Definitional disputes could delay any clean 'AGI achieved' declaration
Possible scaling plateau or capability ceilings before a declarable milestone

key_uncertainties: Whether a declarable AGI event occurs at all, versus indefinite definitional ambiguity
Whether progress sustains or hits a multi-year plateau within the window
update_triggers: Revise UP on clear agentic/general capability breakthroughs or an explicit lab declaration
Revise DOWN on a sustained multi-year capability plateau

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 8%. AEI's 18 June 2026 update and prediction markets (Polymarket ~99.6% 'no invasion by 30 June 2026') indicate Beijing continues to favour gray-zone coercion over a >72hr blockade or assault. US intelligence (March 2026) judges China lacks a fixed timeline and views amphibious operations as extremely difficult; Taiwan's own drills flag 2027 as the salient risk window, which keeps cumulative 2030 odds non-trivial but low.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: onset of a major interstate blockade/invasion within a ~3.5-year window given heavy deterrence and no detected mobilisation. Such transitions are rare; base ~5-10%, with the lower bar (a >72hr blockade) lifting it modestly above a pure-invasion base.

factors_up.factor: 2027 PLA modernisation milestone and sustained large-scale drills near key chokepoints
Blockade (>72hr) is a materially lower threshold than full invasion

factors_down.factor: No detectable amphibious/mobilisation build-up; markets near 99.6% 'no' near-term
Beijing's revealed preference for gray-zone pressure and high costs of US intervention

key_uncertainties: Whether Beijing escalates a gray-zone action past the >72hr blockade threshold
How a 2027-28 leadership/modernisation milestone shifts risk appetite
update_triggers: Revise UP on detected amphibious mobilisation or a declared quarantine/blockade
Revise DOWN on cross-strait de-escalation or credible deterrence reinforcement

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Lowered from 8% to 6% on the May 2026 CPI print (released this week): headline held at 2.8%, but services inflation jumped to 3.7% (from 3.2%) and core rose to 2.6%. With only ~7 monthly prints left before Jan 2027 and underlying services momentum strengthening, a single sub-2.0% month is now even less likely than yesterday's read implied.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: probability that headline CPI prints below a threshold ~0.8pp under the current rate within ~7 months, given sticky services inflation. Rare without a demand shock; base ~5-12%.

factors_up.factor: A sharp energy/food downside shock could pull a single monthly print down quickly
Base effects in late-2026 months could mechanically lower the annual rate

factors_down.factor: Services inflation surged to 3.7% and core to 2.6% — strong stickiness
Headline 2.8% is ~0.8pp above target with few prints remaining

key_uncertainties: Whether an energy/commodity shock materially undercuts a late-2026 monthly print
How quickly services disinflation resumes, if at all
update_triggers: Revise UP if a monthly CPI print drops toward 2.2-2.3% or energy prices fall sharply
Revise DOWN if services inflation stays at/above 3.5%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Raised from 80% to 82% on exceptionally strong pre-sales. Ahead of the 31 July 2026 release, the film posted the second-biggest first-day US pre-sale launch of the post-pandemic era (behind only Taylor Swift's concert film) and is the Polymarket favourite (~54.5%) to be 2026's top domestic earner. Tracker projections span ~$1.5B to ~$2.5B worldwide, with several pointing toward ~$2B — supporting a high probability of clearing $1.5B by year-end given the ~5-month runway.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: MCU Spider-Man / top-tier Marvel tentpoles clearing $1.5B worldwide. No Way Home did ~$1.9B; multiple MCU films cleared $1.5B+. Base ~60-70% for a hyped MCU Spider-Man entry, lifted by record pre-sales.

factors_up.factor: Record-tier pre-sales and No Way Home-level hype with a 'farewell to Peter Parker' hook
~5 months of release runway before the 31 Dec 2026 cutoff

factors_down.factor: $1.5B is a high absolute bar only a handful of films reach
Reception/competition risk could compress legs from blockbuster pre-sale highs

update_triggers: Revise UP after a record-setting opening weekend
Revise DOWN on weak reviews or a soft opening relative to pre-sales

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 98%. June 2026 reporting puts OpenAI's run-rate around $24-25B (filed confidentially for IPO on 8 June 2026) and Anthropic's at roughly $45-47B (up from $9B at end-2025, reportedly doubling on a ~6-week cadence). Their combined run-rate is already near or above $70B mid-year, so clearing the $70B Q4 2026 threshold is near-certain barring a severe reversal.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: probability that a metric already at/near a threshold and growing fast clears it ~6 months later. Conditional on current trajectory, base >90%.

factors_up.factor: Combined mid-2026 run-rate already ~$70B with both firms growing rapidly
Anthropic's reported ~6-week ARR doubling cadence provides large headroom

factors_down.factor: Run-rate figures are self-reported and definitionally noisy
Tail risk of a demand/funding shock or growth stall by Q4

key_uncertainties: Exact Q4 2026 ARR figures each firm/credible outlet reports
Whether reported 'ARR/run-rate' definitions are accepted by the resolver
update_triggers: Revise DOWN if either firm's growth visibly stalls or reporting is sharply revised
Revise UP (toward ceiling) on fresh Q3 prints confirming combined >$70B

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 39%. The OBR's March 2026 outlook assumes medium-term productivity growth of ~1% and labour-supply growth falling to ~0.5% by 2030 — implying potential output growth near 1.5%, right at the threshold — while the IFS is more pessimistic (TFP ~0.4% by 2030). A 10-year arithmetic mean above 1.5% is plausible but hinges on a productivity pickup that is far from assured.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: realised UK decade-average real GDP growth versus a 1.5% bar. The 2010s averaged ~1.8-2.0% but the post-2008 trend has weakened; recent forecasts cluster around 1.1-1.6%. Base ~35-45%.

factors_up.factor: OBR potential-growth assumptions (~1% productivity + ~0.5% labour) sum near 1.5%
Possible AI-driven productivity upside over a full decade

factors_down.factor: Persistent weak trend productivity (IFS ~0.4% TFP); per-person growth only ~1.1%
Declining labour-supply growth and demographic drag through the 2030s

key_uncertainties: Whether a productivity revival (incl. AI diffusion) materialises this decade
Net migration / labour-supply path and its effect on headline GDP growth
update_triggers: Revise UP on sustained productivity acceleration or stronger potential-growth estimates
Revise DOWN if trend productivity stays near 0.3-0.5%
